leads.name: London Plane at the Reservoir (Bridle Path near East 96th Street)

location.address: Bridle Path, east side of the Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir, near East 96th Street, Central Park, New York

leads.reason: NYC Parks Great Trees register: 95.94 feet tall, trunk diameter over 5 feet, possibly planted when the Reservoir was excavated in 1862, called Central Park's oldest tree by Untapped Cities. A strong standalone candidate (two sources: NYC Parks register + Untapped Cities guide) but not pursued to full verification this pass because it sits roughly 1.9km from the nyc_002 (Ramble)/nyc_011-013 cluster this pass was built around, too far to fold into the same walk. Worth a follow-up pass anchored at the Reservoir/96th St instead, possibly paired with the nearby Yoshino Cherries and East 97th St elm below.

leads.name: Yoshino Cherries at the Reservoir (east side, near East 87th Street)

location.address: East side of the Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir, near East 87th Street, Central Park, New York

leads.reason: NYC Parks Great Trees register: part of Japan's 1912 gift of cherry trees to the United States, distinct from the Kwanzan cherries on the reservoir's west side, blooms mid-April. An ensemble candidate similar in kind to the Mall elm allee (nyc_013 in the verified batch), but roughly 1.1-1.2km from the nyc_002 Ramble anchor, stretching the cluster further than the three delivered this pass. Not pursued to full verification for time; a real candidate for a second, more northerly Central Park cluster together with the Reservoir London Plane and East 97th St elm above/below.
leads.location_precision_note: would need a mapped reference point for 'east side near 87th St', not yet found

leads.name: American Elm at East 97th Street entrance

location.address: Near the East 97th Street entrance, Central Park, New York

leads.reason: NYC Parks Great Trees register (id=46): 94.3 feet tall with an 80-foot canopy, dates to the 1800s per NYC Parks, survived Dutch elm disease and 'major superstorms', described as the northernmost Great Tree in the park. Two sources exist (NYC Parks register + Westside Rag/Untapped Cities coverage) but, like the Reservoir trees above, it sits well over 1.5km from the Ramble cluster this pass focused on. Good candidate for the same northerly follow-up cluster.

leads.name: Evodia by Heckscher Playground

location.address: By Heckscher Playground, near Columbus Circle, southern end of Central Park, New York

leads.reason: NYC Parks Great Trees register (id=44): 77.9 feet tall, native to China/Korea, distinctive leaning trunk and fern-like leaves, called 'the hardest NYC Great Tree to track down.' Well documented (register + dedicated tumblr post) but sits at the opposite (south) end of the park from the Ramble/Mall cluster, roughly 2km+ away. A fine standalone tree or seed for a future south-park cluster (with the West Drive area), not part of this pass's cluster.

leads.name: Prospect Park Midwood / Ravine old-growth forest (unnamed individual trees)
leads.species: Tulip Tree (Liriodendron tulipifera), oaks (Quercus spp.), Sweetgum (Liquidambar styraciflua), mixed

location.address: The Midwood and the Ravine, Prospect Park, Brooklyn

leads.reason: Prospect Park Alliance and the Old Growth Forest Network both describe the Midwood/Ravine as Brooklyn's last old-growth upland forest and its oldest trees, dominated by tulip trees around the Midwood and oaks/tulip trees/sweetgums around the Ravine. This pass could not find any INDIVIDUALLY named or singled-out specimen tree within this area (unlike, say, the Camperdown Elm, nyc_003, which already anchors Prospect Park) -- every source describes the forest as a whole, which reads as 'a whole wood' rather than one collectible point per the ensemble test. Not pursued further. A future pass with more time could search Prospect Park Alliance's own tree-tour PDFs or press coverage of specific champion specimens (e.g. a named oldest oak) inside the Ravine/Midwood, which would be a strong Camperdown Elm-adjacent cluster if found.

blocked.name: Arthur Ross Pinetum

location.address: Near the 86th Street entrance / north end of the Great Lawn, Central Park, New York

blocked.reason: A planted collection of roughly 600 pine/conifer trees across 17 species, started 1971 and still expanding by about 35 trees a year. This is a whole grove/collection, not one collectible point and not a compact famous ensemble with one obvious place to stand (it is a several-acre landscaped pinetum, closer to 'a whole wood' than to the Meiji Jingu Gaien avenue precedent). Blocked as not a single collectible point; a genuinely standout individual specimen conifer within it could be reconsidered separately if named.
